Every number has a size; some are small. The method comparison uses twenty of one hundred ten public test cases. That is a sample, not the full set. The twenty seventeen winner line is measured on all one hundred ten.

Clara's U-Net numbers mix challenge training and test cases. They are not a leaderboard result. The per-type table uses thirty two synthetic tasks; several types hit the ceiling. It ranks hub models coarsely.

System One routing used sixty labelled jobs. On October twenty ninth, with six types, accuracy was zero point six eight at coverage zero point six two. Mostly, hard jobs were read as research, which maps to the same model. The thirteen task test is small; it ranks, not benchmarks.

The System One gate used one hundred fifty four commands, labelled by one rater with a rubric written before any model ran. Live since October twenty ninth, it still escalates many harmless commands. Its answer verdicts are unchecked.
Patient data and in-house cohort results stay on the machine. Only public dataset work is published. The quality control runs on the WMH Segmentation Challenge, from Utrecht, Singapore and Amsterdam.

This covers everything derived from such data. A mask, embedding, log line, quality control page, or a model trained on it carries its source class. Comparisons on the mixed pool of challenge and in-house cohorts are missing here, though they are in the wiki. Before every push, a check runs: every dataset needs an explicit release, and a path to unreleased data aborts the push.
